text:
incident-bot: ALERT: multiple pods reporting 'CUDA illegal memory access' and kernel pagewalk misalignment; severity P0. Paging eng-oncall and eng-sre.

Sam (eng-oncall): woke up to pages. seeing ~15% 5xx on /v1/stream and a cluster of pods in CrashLoopBackOff. starting triage.

Ravi (eng-runtime): thumbs up, joining. initial glance: a deployment finished @ 02:10 UTC pushing runtime v2.20. Node logs show 'misaligned address' prints from gpu_mmu.c.

Lina (eng-sre): cluster-autoscaler noticed node flaps; autoscaler kept replacing but new nodes immediately hit the same crash. cordoning affected hosts now (us-west-2).

Sam (eng-oncall): can we stop the rollout?

deploy-bot: STOP ROLLING: tx 9012 (runtime v2.20) halted.

Ravi (eng-runtime): running quick grep:```
grep -R "misaligned addr" /var/log/pods/* -n | head -n 20
# sample backtrace snippet
# gpu_mmu.c:789: pagewalk_fetch+0x1d8
# inference_worker.c:402: kv_fetch
```

Anya (eng-platform): creating routing rule to steer heavy models to safe-pool (runtime v2.18). Applying now.

Taylor (cs): flagging customers: two Dedicated customers reported errors, one raised a support incident. crafting a short customer note.

Marco (support): ticketed: SUP-4219, SUP-4220. customers include high-throughput inference jobs — they're seeing retries. adding incident link.

Ravi (eng-runtime): quick mitigation: disable async prefetch flag (ENV: KV_ASYNC_PREFETCH=false) and restart workers on canary nodes. flipping now.

Lina (eng-sre): after toggling KV_ASYNC_PREFETCH on canary (3 nodes), no new illegal-access crashes in 8m. autoscaler still trying to add nodes, but we'll keep them cordoned.

incident-bot: ONCALL HANDOFF scheduled: Sam -> Ravi at 03:05 UTC.

Sam (eng-oncall): handing to Ravi for root cause and vendor escalation. collected core dumps and nvlog bundles to s3://incidents/2832123456/. note: some pods OOM'ed before the illegal-access messages.

Ravi (eng-runtime): deeper dive: reproducer attempt: run 70B with long context and repeated batch eviction. memcheck shows unaligned PTE read during rapid KV evict + reuse. suspect race in our prefetcher touching stale device pointers.

VendorBot: case opened with GPU vendor #VB-5573 (attached logs). vendor requested pci device mapping info and minisys traces.

Anya (eng-platform): also adding a temporary admission control: deny >8 concurrent streams for 70B models on pools running v2.20. route to slower pool otherwise.

Taylor (cs): customer note draft: "We're investigating intermittent GPU runtime crashes impacting large-model requests. We've isolated affected nodes and rerouted traffic; disabling a new prefetch optimization to reduce risk. We'll follow up with a technical postmortem."

Marco (support): posted to customers affected. one large customer acknowledged and asked for ETA.

Ravi (eng-runtime): proposed plan: 1) keep rollout paused 2) roll runtime back on a small canary 3) run synthetic eviction stress test + memcheck 4) vendor deep-dive on driver alignment behavior.

Lina (eng-sre): executed cordon on 6 nodes, drained 4. scheduling maintenance to push v2.18/2.19 or patch at 05:30 UTC.

Ravi (eng-runtime): added a short-term crash detector in the agent: if 'misaligned' seen twice in 60s, auto-fence new incoming KV-prefetch requests and flip KV_ASYNC_PREFETCH=false on that node. will push in 5m.

Sam (eng-oncall): nice. that should limit blast radius. leaving for sleep; Ravi you have the handoff. :zzz: please update if anything regresses.

Ravi (eng-runtime): flipping detector now and pushing canary rollback to v2.18 on 3 nodes.

deploy-bot: Rolling update: runtime v2.20 -> v2.18 on canary nodes (3).

Ravi (eng-runtime): canary looks stable for 12m with detector + prefetch disabled. no further OOMs/crashes.

VendorBot: vendor replied: driver team suspects PTE-format change in driver X. They requested a minimal reproducer and kernel vtable dumps.

Anya (eng-platform): routing policy in place so high-memory requests go to v2.18 pool. adding a feature flag to control prefetch globally (PLAT-1737).

Taylor (cs): customers updated. one asked for rollback timing to all Dedicated pools; we're estimating a safe rollout after thorough stress testing.

Marco (support): consolidating related tickets and linking to INC-2832123456. closing duplicates.

Ravi (eng-runtime): next steps: build deterministic reproducer for vendor, add regression test for concurrent eviction + prefetch, and add an auto-fallback at the load-balancer when a node shows misaligned traces.

Lina (eng-sre): incident timeline notes: trigger 02:10 UTC (v2.20 rollout) -> first crashes 02:12 -> cordon 02:18 -> canary rollback & toggle 02:28 -> mitigation effective 02:40. scheduling postmortem doc.

Sam (eng-oncall): marking incident mitigated; severity down to P2. leave thread open for postmortem draft. good work everyone. :thumbsup:

Ravi (eng-runtime): uploading artifacts: /tmp/coredumps/* -> s3://incidents/2832123456/artifacts/. added gdb backtraces and memcheck logs.

Taylor (cs): storing customer comms: s3://incidents/2832123456/customer_updates.md

Lina (eng-sre): created PM issue and assigned owners: PM-INC-2832123456. draft EOD.

Ravi (eng-runtime): remember to add a metric alert for 'misaligned access rate' so we can auto-throttle deployments in future.

incident-bot: THREAD ARCHIVED (auto)  artifacts saved to INC-2832123456."
